text:
ops-bot: INCIDENT [P1] hosted-api: unexpected request surge -> GPU queue growth, p95/p99 latency spike, autoscaler not provisioning. link: https://internal/redwood/incidents/9187654321 :rotating_light:

tim (oncall): seeing p99 tokens jump to ~12s, queue depth 65k in us-west-1. Automated alerts for GPU pool saturation. I'm paged and looking.

alice (eng-runtime): confirmed. Metrics: model-serving-cpu/gpu_utilization=98%; provisioner-queue-length rising. Autoscaler logs show repeated create attempts failing with 429 from cloud quota API.

carla (eng-infra): getting quota errors: "ExceededResourceQuota: Cannot create more GPU instances in us-west-1". There's a soft limit applied by finance for burst accounts. Opening console now.

amy (support): got tickets from 3 customers complaining about timeouts and 504s. Tiered customers: two enterprise customers affected. Need ETA to reply.

michael (sre): this looks like a twofold failure: real traffic spike + autoscaler blocked by quota. Short-term: throttle heavy traffic and route known enterprise tenants to reserved pools if possible. Longer: request quota increase and manual provisioning.

tim (oncall): steps I'm taking: 1) enable emergency rate-limiter at edge for unauthenticated/bursty routes, 2) flip fallback routing to smaller-latency model variants for non-enterprise tenants, 3) try manual scale of dedicated pool for enterprise tenants.

alice (eng-runtime): suggested commands:
```
# temporarily reduce burst window
curl -X POST https://infra-api.internal/ratelimit/edge -d '{"global_rate": "2000r/s", "burst": 1000}'
# fallback routing toggle
curl -X POST https://router.internal/override -d '{"route":"/v1/generate","policy":"fallback-small-models"}'
```

carla (eng-infra): manual instance creation failing with same quota error. I can allocate from eu-west if cross-region is acceptable, but will increase latency for EU customers.

tim (oncall): prioritize: 1) keep enterprise customers on stable reserved pools (if available), 2) open a quota escalation with cloud (I've initiated support ticket), 3) apply edge throttles to reduce new queue ingress.

amy (support): drafting customer-facing message for the two affected customers. Need expected ETA for mitigation. If we can route them to dedicated, shareholders ask for 10-15m estimate.

michael (sre): quick mitigation executed: enabled edge limit for anonymous & guest tokens, set per-tenant cap for top-10 highest QPS tenants. Also enabled prefix KV cache for frequent requests to reduce token costs.

ops-bot: Action logged: mitigation.edge_rate_limit=true by tim (9187654400); mitigation.fallback_routing=true by alice (9187654410). Incident assigned to tim (oncall).

alice (eng-runtime): noticed a backlog consumer in the provisioner leader loop: repeated leader election restarts correlated with provisioning requests. Dump: 
```
2026-03-16T20:40:12Z provisioner leader lost lease: conflict
2026-03-16T20:40:13Z attempt create-gpu-instance -> 429 QuotaExceeded
2026-03-16T20:40:15Z leader restart
```

carla (eng-infra): cloud team responded to our ticket: quota can be increased but takes 45-90 minutes if expedited. They've asked for justification. I'm requesting an immediate soft-limit override for our infra key.

tim (oncall): short-term routing: i've flipped the route to send enterprise customer IDs to our reserved dedicated pool (manual override). That should reduce timeouts for them. Non-enterprise remains throttled.

amy (support): sending update to customers: "We're aware of increased errors for hosted API in us-west-1; we've routed enterprise workloads to reserved capacity and applied temporary rate limits to reduce errors. Engineers are working on restoring normal capacity; ETA ~30-45m."

michael (sre): monitoring: after edge throttle, incoming QPS dropped ~35%, queue growth slowed but still positive. p95 improved from 4s -> 2.1s; p99 still elevated ~8s due to backlog.

alice (eng-runtime): running emergency backfill consumers to drain KV-cache warmups and increase worker parallelism where safe. Watch for higher OOM risk.

carla (eng-infra): cloud granted a short-lived quota bump for +4 GPUs in us-west-1 while they process the full increase. I started manual provisioning of those instances.

ops-bot: Provisioner event: created 4 extra gpus (ids: gpu-az1-345, gpu-az1-346, gpu-az2-112, gpu-az2-113) by carla at 9187654520.

tim (oncall): after the 4 GPUs came up, queue drained noticeably. p99 dropped to ~3.2s and errors <2%. Continuing to monitor for 30m.

amy (support): updated customers with mitigation note and that enterprise routing is complete. They replied thanks, will monitor.

michael (sre): follow-ups for postmortem: a) autoscaler should surface quota errors as SLI to oncall, b) provisioner leader election needs hardened backoff to avoid restart storms, c) we need a pre-authorized burst quota for critical regions.

alice (eng-runtime): also propose: smarter admission control that enforces per-tenant soft quotas earlier in request pipeline to avoid bulk queueing.

carla (eng-infra): next actions: submit formal quota increase request (ticket opened), add alert on cloud quota 80% utilization, and add runbook step to fallback cross-region for EU/US customers.

tim (oncall): incident status -> mitigated, monitoring. Tagging for postmortem and handoff to day shift. If anything regresses, page SRE. :white_check_mark:

ops-bot: Incident status: mitigated. Duration: ~55m. Assigned postmortem: eng-runtime + eng-infra.

amy (support): closing customer tickets as 'monitoring' and logging follow-up with account execs.

michael (sre): documenting timeline and metrics for postmortem. Will attach logs and autoscaler traces.

alice (eng-runtime): adding backlog replay scripts and the list of affected tenant IDs to the postmortem doc.

tim (oncall): handing off to day shift @michael (sre) and @carla (eng-infra) for remediation work. I'll update oncall channel if anything else pops.

michael (sre): acknowledged, will take lead on postmortem and quotas.

carla (eng-infra): acknowledged, will own quota escalation and runbook changes.

ops-bot: Thread closed (auto) at 9187654555.
